description: Clause cases merged from the clause-case files of carve-js, carve-php and carve-rs (next2), each kept only where a clause decides it; why quotes the deciding sentence. Curated by hand. See README.md.

cases.why: C2-B-130: A line of a line block keeps the spaces that lead it after the strip (C2-B-027) as content (carried over from 0.1).
cases.summary: indented line block keeps leading space

cases.why: C2-B-130: A line of a line block keeps the spaces that lead it after the strip (C2-B-027) as content (carried over from 0.1). C2-B-123: The body of a line block is one leaf that recognizes only prefixes, the closer and a comment block (C2-B-108): every other line is a line of text.
cases.summary: line block in quote in item keeps tab

cases.why: C2-B-119: Behind those spaces a sigil starts a sigil div also when further words are glued to it, and C2-B-122 reports the words: `::: >a` opens a quote fence.
cases.summary: sigil with glued words opens empty line block

cases.why: C2-B-225: Where it is not a space, a valid attribute block there is an attribute block (C2-B-105), and any other character, a brace block that is no valid attribute block included (C2-I-028 to C2-I-034), starts further words (C2-B-122).
cases.summary: attribute block glued to div name not applied

cases.why: C2-H-166: For `max_nesting` the children of the document stand at level 0, and each block level and each inline level below adds one. A node at a level above the bound is outside the profile; a node at the bound stays, and its children are degraded.
cases.summary: comment profile nesting bound degrades code span

cases.why: C2-H-165: every other inline node with no children as the writer spells that node on its own (C2-W-116), since a tree holds no source text.
cases.summary: comment profile degrades inline math to source spelling

cases.why: C2-A-084: Its panels are the tables among its children, and the image paragraphs, code blocks, quotes and math blocks among them that carry a caption; there is no separate panel list.
cases.summary: nested figure group is no panel, caption numbered

cases.why: C2-A-049: It carries `format`, which is the word on its opener or `"yaml"` when there is none, and `value`, the text between the delimiters as written, which ends with a line break after its last line also where the block is unclosed and the source ends there without one (C2-A-046).
cases.summary: unclosed frontmatter keeps trailing whitespace line

cases.why: C2-B-171: A cell prefix is the optional header cell mark `|=`, then an optional run of glued brace blocks, merged into one (C2-B-093). C2-I-034: One part that fits no shape makes the whole run no attribute block.
cases.summary: cell prefix stops at invalid brace block

cases.why: C2-B-225: The first character behind the run that is not one of them ends the run; it is part of no name.
cases.summary: figure name with glued words gives figure group

cases.why: C2-B-043: A bare dot is no marker when the text behind its required space starts with another dot and a space, so `. . . and then silence` is a paragraph.
cases.summary: bare dot before spaced dot is text

cases.why: C2-H-165: A node that leaves no text is dropped.
cases.summary: minimal profile drops empty degraded table

cases.why: C2-I-076: A reference label is the run of characters up to the next `]` that no backslash escapes.
cases.summary: label ends at first bracket, no block image

cases.why: C2-I-079: A label whose key is empty after folding, one that holds only spaces, tabs or a line break, is no label: the brackets are text.
cases.summary: blank image label is text, no caption

cases.why: C2-I-078: A label whose first character is an at-sign is not a reference label. C2-I-101: The brackets are text and the key is read as a mention (C2-I-078, C2-I-090).
cases.summary: at-sign label is no reference, mention

cases.why: C2-I-077: Atoms are read first, so a line comment that starts inside a label takes the rest of its line (C2-I-024): the label is unclosed and the brackets are text.
cases.summary: line comment in image label, no image

cases.why: C2-I-024: A line comment takes the rest of its line with every closer on it.
cases.summary: line comment in image alt, no image

cases.why:
C2-B-197: A block image line is decided by its shape and not by inline parsing: the line consists of exactly one image form, `![alt](destination)`, `![alt][label]` or the collapsed `![alt][]`, optional attribute blocks glued to it (C2-I-039), and trailing spaces. C2-H-020: Where the image is an unresolved reference, C2-H-085 writes it as text, and text needs a block around it: the paragraph then keeps its `

`.
cases.summary: unresolved block image with caption keeps p

cases.why: C2-I-069: A tail with a space in the destination, a broken title or a line break is no tail: the bracket pair is text and the parenthesis is text.
cases.summary: tab after title breaks image tail

cases.why: C2-B-122: An unquoted title or further words in the info string do not stop the block from opening, and `fence-title-syntax` reports them.
cases.summary: spaced brace block after figure ignored

cases.why: C2-H-024: Authored ids are reserved first, in document order. Generated ids follow in document order, and a slug that is already taken gets the suffix `-2`, then `-3`, and so on.
cases.summary: id on unresolved reference reserves slug

cases.why: C2-I-033: A quoted value stands in `"` or `'`.
cases.summary: single-quoted value holding double quote

`.

cases.why: C2-I-118: Inline nesting stops at depth 200 in each inline content, whatever the blocks around it: the count starts at zero where the content starts (C2-I-120), and no block counts (C2-B-190).

cases.why: C2-B-154: A line that is not indented past the marker starts a new block; a comment-only line is no such line (C2-B-137), so its comment is a child of the heading (C2-B-138) and an indented line below it still continues the heading.
cases.summary: comment-only line below heading joins heading

cases.why: C2-B-184: Each fragment is an inline content by itself (C2-B-223), so every inline form opens and closes inside one physical row, and an opener whose closer is not in its own fragment is text, as at the end of a cell.
cases.summary: emphasis cannot span continuation row fragments

cases.why: C2-I-104: A quote opens when the neighbor before it is whitespace or opening punctuation, or when it has none because the quote stands at the start of the content or directly behind an opening mark or bracket. Otherwise it closes, also directly behind a closing mark, a closing bracket or an atom.
cases.summary: smart quotes read from neighbors, apostrophe before digit

cases.why:
C2-H-133: It renders as a paragraph that holds the directive as text, written bare or with `

` as a `paragraph` node at its place would be (C2-H-006, C2-H-007, C2-H-034, C2-H-040): `{{`, a space, the path as C2-H-171 writes it, the section, the options in the order of C2-W-058 and the entries of `invalid` as the tree holds them, each after one space, a space and `}}`.
cases.summary: unexpanded include keeps invalid options as written

cases.why: C2-B-172: A `<` in the first column, a `<` whose left cell is covered by a row span from above, a `^` in the first row of its group and a `^` below a cell that spans more than one column join nothing (C2-B-173): in `|a|<|` above `|^|b|`, the `^` is the text of its cell.
cases.summary: span mark at first row of body and foot

cases.why: C2-B-209: A count larger than the number of rows is the number of rows, so every row is in the head, and `table-row-count-clamped` reports the count.
cases.summary: delimited table header-rows clamped to row count

cases.summary: captioned image attributes move to figure

cases.why: C2-A-082: Below a code block, which holds no children, it is the sibling after the block (C2-A-145).
cases.summary: comment between code block and caption

cases.why: C2-B-138: The comment of a comment-only line, and a comment that stands alone after a marker or a quote mark, is a child of the open leaf when one is open, and otherwise a comment node of the innermost open container, whatever the line's indent.
cases.summary: comment between quote and its caption

cases.why: C2-H-096: A resolved cross-reference is `<a href="#ID">` around generated text. ... For a numbered caption it is the label word and the number, such as `Figure 1`.
